as_told.title: Lone gray craft in trouble over the Plains of San Agustin
as_told.place_text: Plains of San Agustin, New Mexico

plain: A flying saucer is said to have crashed in the summer of 1947 on the Plains of San Agustin, a high desert flat in western New Mexico. The story is usually told with dead crew aboard and one alien still alive, though the two guests who mention it here speak only of the craft. The scientist John Brandenburg tells Michels, as something passed on to him, that "roughly the morning of 4th of July an object crashed on the plains of San Augustine about 100 miles away." He sets it in the same days as the better-known Roswell crash. Charles Hall, who says he spent three years with tall white aliens at Area 51, brings it up as a point of comparison. He describes a craft that is "in deep trouble," "as in the craft over the sand plains of San Augustine in 1947." If true, it would mean that more than one craft came down in New Mexico that summer.
